clauses.mechanism: express revocation by EO 12553: its operative sentence ends with the words "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and is followed by a two-column table headed 'No. Subject' whose entry "11303 Modifying provisions for transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations" names this order by number; EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the full held text was searched for effective, take effect, except, provided, saving, nothing and pending), so the revocation is read as taking effect on signing, February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986; filed February 26, 1986). The signing-date reading is an inference from the order's heading and signature block, not express wording.
clauses.reason: whole: The order waives, for one named employee, the limit in section 1 of EO 9721 on the period treated as leave of absence and deems him on leave from March 9, 1954 through September 12, 1957 for the purposes of EO 9721. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes it by number ("11303 Modifying provisions for transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations"). The waiver took effect on the order's own date (1966-09-12), a disclosed alternative reading of exhaustion that is not adopted as the end because the deeming operates for the rights and benefits provided by EO 9721, which remained in force until the same revocation. The surviving consequence is recorded under savings.

research_rationale:
EO 11303 (1966-09-12, 31 FR 11963) modifies EO 9721, as amended by EO 10103, by waiving for Reginald C. Price the limitation in section 1 on the period during which an employee is considered on leave of absence, and deeming him on leave from March 9, 1954 through September 12, 1957 for the purpose of all rights and benefits under EO 9721. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11303.txt, 31 FR 11963, PDF pages 5-5) and confirmed its number, title and date against the census register. The order is a single paragraph with one operative command, so the dossier's single clause is the complete inventory. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25) revokes EO 11303 by number (row "11303 Modifying provisions for transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations") and also lists EO 9721. The first end is that express revocation. The waiver is a one-person act that took effect on the order's date; under the owner ruling of 2026-10-28 the exhausted waiver is distinguished from the surviving consequence (the credited leave period and the rights that rest on it), and no held source shows an earlier cessation of the command. The alternative reading, that the self-executing deeming was exhausted when the order took effect on 1966-09-12, is disclosed for the reviewer; I did not adopt it because the deeming operates 'for the purpose of all rights and benefits provided by' EO 9721, which stayed in force until EO 12553 revoked it. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).

Disclosed alternative end (not adopted): 1966-09-12, the order's own date, if the self-executing waiver is treated as exhausted when it took effect.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order contains only the waiver and deeming for one named person; it creates no appointment, fund or delegation. savings.reason: EO 12553 has no savings, exception, pending-matter or 'nothing herein' wording (searched in the full held text), so the revocation does not preserve the order as a command. The credited leave period for the named employee and any rights and benefits that accrued under EO 9721 while it was in force are accrued consequences; the held sources do not show any open claim.
